pc_bridge_hint: Translate into an intermediate locale first, then from that locale into each target. This two-step approach can improve quality for language pairs where direct translation data is scarce in smaller models.

pc_bridge_en_d: Source → English → target. Recommended when the source is not English.

pc_source_hint: The language strings are written in. Must not appear in targets.

pc_bridge_store_hint: A bridge locale that is a target is always stored.
pc_pivot_hint: Some locale variants are better translated from a related locale than from the source — for example pt-BR from pt-PT. A pivot overrides the bridge for that locale.
pc_shared_hint: A shared glossary is defined once and used by multiple projects — brand terms, product names and technical vocabulary that must stay consistent.
pc_attach: Attach a shared glossary from another project:

mkt_footer_lede: Open-source localisation engine: find hardcoded strings, translate with a local or cloud engine, validate, review. MIT licensed.
mkt_badge_oss: Open source · MIT license · local or cloud
mkt_hero_h1_b: Translate with Claude, GPT, DeepSeek or your own GPU.
mkt_hero_lede: llm-localizator finds UI text that never made it into a catalogue, translates it with the engine you pick, checks every placeholder and plural, and gives you a review panel. Local or cloud, your choice: nothing leaves your machine unless you pick a cloud engine.
mkt_features_h2: From hardcoded text to reviewed translations.
mkt_features_lede: One tool for the whole loop. Validation and the scanner need no model; translation runs on the engine you choose.
mkt_how_h2: From zero to shipped in four commands.
mkt_formats_lede: Adapters read and write each format in place and convert to ICU messages internally, so validation and prompts see one shape whatever is on disk.
mkt_install_lede: Python 3.12 or newer. Validation, the scanner and the review UI work without any model. Add Ollama for local engines or an API key for a cloud engine.
mkt_cta_lede: Run it on your own machine with a local model, or point it at a cloud engine billed to your own API key. No per-seat or per-word fees from us.
mkt_how_sub: Four steps from source code to reviewed, shipped translations.
mkt_tools_lede: Both run in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.
mkt_pipeline_discover_body: init registers your catalogues; agent-hardcoded lists UI text still hardcoded in source, with a confidence tier per hit.
mkt_pipeline_translate_body: Pick an engine (local Ollama tier or a cloud model) and translate missing keys; long sweeps can run through a job queue.
mkt_pipeline_validate_body: Placeholders, ICU plurals, tags and length budgets are checked with no model. check-keys runs in CI.
mkt_pipeline_review_body: Edit, compare locales, see quality scores and approve in the local review UI.
mkt_roadmap_lede: What is shipped, what is being measured, and what comes next.
mkt_api_lede: The local review server exposes the endpoints the web UI uses: push source strings, pull translations, run operations. It binds to your machine; POSTs need the session token printed at startup. Cloud engines stay opt-in.
mkt_tools_prices: Rough estimate (4 characters per token). Prices as of {as_of}.
mkt_feat_01_b: Scans source for UI text that bypasses your catalogue and tags each hit high, medium or low confidence. Built for precision: treat it as a worklist, not a verdict.
mkt_feat_02_b: A local web editor: side-by-side locales, quality scores, translation memory, comments, history and revert.
mkt_feat_03_b: One switch sets every role. Local tiers for 4, 8 and 16 GB GPUs, or Claude, DeepSeek and OpenAI. Cloud runs show a cost estimate first.
mkt_feat_04_b: A CLI for every step, a job queue for long sweeps, check-keys for CI, an agent backlog and an MCP server for coding agents.
mkt_feat_05_b: Placeholders, ICU plurals, markup and length budgets checked on every string, with no model. Rescore without re-translating.
mkt_feat_06_b: JSON, YAML, gettext, ARB, Android, iOS, Xcode string catalogs, XLIFF, RESX, Qt and more, read and written in place.
mkt_how_01_b: Detects your catalogue format and writes a .llm-localize.toml config.
mkt_how_02_b: List hardcoded UI text, then check placeholders, ICU and length budgets. No model needed; safe in CI.
mkt_how_03_b: Pick an engine for your hardware or budget, then fill the missing keys.
mkt_how_04_b: Open the review UI. Score, edit, approve. Commit and ship.
mkt_cta_1: Local engines: strings never leave your machine
mkt_cta_3: Cloud engines are opt-in, with a budget you set
mkt_cta_4: Validation and scanning work offline, no model needed
mkt_req_3: API key optional (Claude, DeepSeek or OpenAI engines)
mkt_web_opens: review UI opens in your browser
mkt_meta_title: llm-localizator — find hardcoded strings & localize with AI
mkt_meta_description: Open-source localisation engine: finds hardcoded UI strings, translates with Claude, GPT, DeepSeek or a local Ollama model, validates placeholders and plurals, and gives you a review UI. MIT licensed.
mkt_engines_lede: An engine sets the model for every role: translate, back-translate, score, improve. Local engines run on Ollama and keep every string on your machine; cloud engines need your API key and an explicit opt-in.
mkt_engines_status_note: Status is the evidence behind each engine: benchmarked in a model bakeoff, accepted on a waiver after a smoke test, smoke-tested only, or not benchmarked yet.
mkt_bench_h2: Measured on code we did not write.
mkt_bench_lede: The scanner is tuned on development projects and scored once on held-out third-party projects labelled by agents that never saw its output. It is precise; it does not find everything.
mkt_bench_projects: held-out real open-source projects in seven rounds, picked for unusual text storage (Chrome extensions, Godot, Rails/HAML, Go TUIs, Discord bots and more)
mkt_bench_recall: macro recall: it finds about three in five of the labelled text in these rounds, so expect misses
mkt_bench_tier_supported: Supported (held-out bar met): JavaScript, TSX, HTML, Vue, Svelte, Astro, ERB, XML UI files and Godot scenes.
mkt_bench_tier_basic: Basic: Python, Dart, Kotlin, C#, Rust, Swift and others. Hits come with a confidence tier; review them.
mkt_bench_tier_gaps: Not scanned yet: HAML, Slim and MDX views. The report lists every language it skipped.
mkt_bench_method: Held-out rounds of 2026-11-14, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17 (scanner v57 to v67). Per-project numbers and tier rules:
mkt_fmt_multilang_json: All locales in one JSON file
